content.title: Nothing Bundt Cakes Reportedly Sold, and Duke’s Boozer Brothers Team Up for Zaxbys
content.text: The Boozer brothers, Cameron (left) and Cayden (right), along with Duke University basketball teammate Nik Khamenia (center), teamed up with Zaxbys to promote its new dry rub menu items in celebration of March Madness. Duke takes on St. John's University tonight in the NCAA's Sweet 16. FT’s Picks of the Week highlight notable C-suite moves, brand milestones, tech tidbits and other franchise news, sourced by the Franchise Times editorial team.Private equity firm KKR agreed to acquire bakery chain Nothing Bundt Cakes from Roark Capital for more than $2 billion, including debt, according to The Wall Street Journal and Reuters, marking a major sale for the fast-growing franchise brand with more than 500 locations across the United States and Canada. Roark—the PE owner of Inspire Brands and GoTo Foods, Subway and Dave’s Hot Chicken—purchased Nothing Bundt Cakes in 2021 from Levine Leichtman Capital Partners. The bakery company has grown quickly in recent years, adding 51 stores in 2022, 84 in 2023 and 101 in 2024 with plans to open more than 100 locations annually going forward. Started by Las Vegas friends Dena Tripp and Debbie Shwetz in 1997, the company is aiming for 1,000 units by 2027. Nothing Bundt Cakes is set to join KKR's portfolio. Nothing Bundt Cakes generates around $850 million in revenue with locations pulling in $1.4 to $1.5 million in annual sales on average and top-performing stores exceeding $2.4 million. According to Reuters, Nothing Bundt Cakes is expected to generate approximately $120 million in earnings in 2026 before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization.Founded by former Bear Stearns employees George Roberts, Henry Kravis and Jerome Kohlberg in 1976, New York City-based KKR is a global investment firm known for acquiring RJR Nabsico for $25 billion in 1989. It manages about $744 billion in assets.Roark was running a sale process for the bakery chain with investment banks ​North Point and Bank of America, ​Reuters reported last year.NotableRogers Mueller is taking over as CEO of RPM Pizza, which is one of Domino’s largest franchisees with 137 locations across Mississippi, Alabama, Louisiana and Indiana. Mueller is the son of Glenn Mueller, who along with his brother Richard Mueller founded RPM Pizza in 1981. The operation grew from a local business into what was at one point the largest Domino’s franchise group in the United States. Mueller died in 2024.A Dunkin’ and Taco Bell franchisee agreed to pay more than $1.5 million in restitution to 760 workers after an investigation found it systemically violated local scheduling laws at 24 Manhattan and Queens, New York locations, according to the New York City Department of Consumer and Worker Protection. A two-year probe by DCWP found that Salz Management arbitrarily changed workers’ schedules and failed to give workers schedules with 14 days notice, which is in violation of the city’s Fair Workweek Law. The Long Island-based company’s franchise portfolio also includes Wingstop, Wendy’s and Baskin Robbins, according to a news report. In partnership with G&J Pepsi and franchisee Robert E. Lee III, Donatos Pizza is providing free meals to TSA workers at John Glenn Columbus International Airport in Ohio. Every Tuesday and Saturday until the shutdown ends, TSA employees can receive a free a 10-inch one-topping pizza and a 20-ounce Pepsi by showing their badge at one of the two Donatos locations inside the airport. Lee has been principal and president of Touchstone Hospitality, a minority-owned full-service hospitality management firm, since 2007. It operates airport concessions, including Donatos, Auntie Anne’s and Starbucks, through partnerships with HMSHost.MilestonesIce cream and frozen custard company Stricklands is celebrating 90 years of business in 2026. Founded in 1936 by Bill and Florence Strickland in Akron, Ohio, the company has six locations, with five stores in its home state of Ohio and one in California.Hydrate IV Bar is marking its 10th anniversary this year. The company has grown to 33 locations in eight states since opening its first location in Denver in 2016. Since launching its franchise system in 2020, the brand has achieved nearly 40 percent average annual growth, accelerating to 100 percent year-over-year growth in 2025, according to the release.Just for funCollege basketball stars and twin brothers Cayden and Cameron Boozer, along with Duke teammate Nik Khamenia, teamed up with Zaxbys to promote its new dry rub menu items in celebration of March Madness. The brand introduced the Boozer Brothers Meal, a digital-exclusive offering created in partnership with the Boozer brothers, who are the sons of former NBA player Carlos Boozer.
